chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can introduce themselves and others, describe nuclear and extended families, and talk about classes and school subjects.

objectifsLesson.description: Say one's name, age, and class.
Use personal pronouns I / you and the verb to be in the present tense.
Pronounce the articles a / an correctly.
Introduce another person (This is..., He/She is...).
Use possessive adjectives my / your / his / her.
Ask simple questions with What's your name? How old are you?
Write and rearrange simple questions and answers.
Use to be and to have (affirmative, negative, interrogative forms).
Use cardinal numbers (1–50) to state age.
Recognize words: mother, father, brother, sister, parents, children.
Read a simple family tree.
Listen to a dialogue to identify family members.

lessons.titreLesson: Describing Relationships in the Nuclear Family

objectifsLesson.description: Use the verb to be to describe (She is my mother).
Use to have to express possession (I have one sister).
Form negative and interrogative sentences.

lessons.titreLesson: Writing and Talking About One's Nuclear Family

objectifsLesson.description: Draw and label one's own family tree.
Rearrange words to form correct sentences.
Orally present one's nuclear family in 3–4 sentences.
Learn words: grandfather, grandmother, uncle, aunt, cousin, nephew, niece.
Distinguish them from nuclear family members.
Read a family tree including three generations.

lessons.titreLesson: Expressing Possession and Relationships in Extended Family

objectifsLesson.description: Use possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers).
Use definite and indefinite articles (a, an, the).
Answer questions like Who is this? / Whose...?

lessons.titreLesson: Describing Extended Family Orally and in Writing

objectifsLesson.description: Write 5–6 sentences about one's extended family.
Ask a classmate questions about their family.
Present a short dialogue based on a family photo.

lessons.titreLesson: Naming School Subjects and Classroom Objects

objectifsLesson.description: Know school subjects: Maths, English, History, Science, PE, Art.
Know classroom objects: desk, board, book, pen, timetable.
Read a simple timetable.

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Talking About School Subjects

objectifsLesson.description: Ask and answer: What's your favourite subject? / When do you have...?
Use days of the week and ordinal numbers (1st, 2nd, etc.).
Listen to a short dialogue between students.

lessons.titreLesson: Expressing Likes and Dislikes at School

objectifsLesson.description: Use I like / I don't like / I love / I hate.
Give simple reasons (because it's interesting/difficult/fun).
Write 3–5 sentences about one's school preferences.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can identify money, ask for locations in a market, buy and sell goods, and describe jobs and professions.

objectifsLesson.description: Recognize and name local currency coins and notes.
Read and understand simple bills and price tags.
Pronounce regular plural forms correctly (s / es).

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Giving Information About Amounts

objectifsLesson.description: Ask and answer questions like How much is it? / How much are they?
Use demonstrative pronouns: this, that, these, those.
Write and fill in simple bills with items and prices.

lessons.titreLesson: Naming Locations Inside a Market or Supermarket

objectifsLesson.description: Learn vocabulary: aisle, shelf, checkout, entrance, dairy section, vegetable section.
Read pictures and identify locations inside a supermarket.
Use prepositions of place (next to, between, opposite, near).

lessons.titreLesson: Asking for and Giving Directions in a Market

objectifsLesson.description: Ask Where can I find...? / Which aisle is...?
Give simple directions (Go straight, turn left/right, it's next to...).
Complete sentences with location expressions.

lessons.titreLesson: Describing Locations in Writing and Speech

objectifsLesson.description: Write 3–4 sentences describing where items are located.
Role-play a customer asking for help and a shop assistant giving directions.
Listen to short descriptions and identify the correct location.
Learn words: groceries, food, clothes, shoes, price, cost, quality, quantity.
Use countable and uncountable nouns (e.g., apples vs. rice).
Use partitives (a bottle of, a kilo of, a piece of).

lessons.titreLesson: Asking About Cost, Quality, and Quantity

objectifsLesson.description: Ask How much does it cost? / How many? / How much?
Use have got (affirmative, negative, interrogative: I have got / Have you got?).
Express likes and dislikes (I like this, I don't want that).
Perform a short dialogue between a seller and a buyer.
Write simple questions and answers about goods and services.
Listen to advertisements and identify key information (price, product, promotion).
Recognize jobs: teacher, doctor, farmer, shopkeeper, nurse, driver.
Read short simple texts with pictures describing jobs.
Pronounce job names correctly with regular plural endings.
Use simple present tense to describe jobs (He teaches. She sells.).
Use can / may to talk about abilities (A doctor can help you. May I help you?)
Answer Who is this? / What does he/she do?
Say I like / I don't like being a...
Describe a dream job in 3–4 sentences.
Write a short paragraph about a job (name, tasks, tools, uniform).
Listen to short dialogues or sketches about professions.
Read simple advertisements or conversations about jobs.
Complete sentences with job-related vocabulary.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can describe times, seasons, weather, common diseases, safety needs, and balanced diets.

lessons.titreLesson: Periods of the Day and Daily Routines

objectifsLesson.description: Learn vocabulary: morning, afternoon, evening, night, sunrise, sunset.
Listen to short dialogues or news reports to identify routines.
Write simple sentences describing daily activities at specific times.
Describe weather: sunny, cloudy, foggy, rainy, windy.
Read simple charts, captions, or tables about weather.
Pronounce weak and strong forms in speech correctly (e.g., and, but, for).
Name the seasons (spring, summer, autumn/fall, winter).
Talk about activities done in each season (swimming, planting, harvesting).
Write 3–4 sentences about a favorite season and its weather.

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Answering About Time and Season

objectifsLesson.description: Use interrogative words: what, which, when, why, how.
Ask When do you wake up? / What is the weather like in summer?
Read simple illustrated texts about seasons and activities.
Learn vocabulary: malaria, cold, cough, fever, headache, stomachache, diarrhea.
Identify basic parts of the body (head, stomach, throat).
Read short simple texts with pictures about diseases and symptoms.
Listen to instructions about consultations and drug prescriptions.
Understand the dangers of self-medication.
Read simple prescriptions or medical instructions.

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Giving Information About Illnesses

objectifsLesson.description: Ask and answer What is wrong? / I have a headache.
Use the simple past of to be, to have, and to do (I was sick, I had a fever).
Write simple questions and answers about common diseases and treatment.
Learn words: wash, soap, clean, trash, waste, toilet, germs, bacteria.
Read slogans, speeches, captions, dialogues, or flyers on hygiene.
Use the simple imperative (Wash your hands. Dispose of trash properly.).

lessons.titreLesson: Safety Rules at Home and School

objectifsLesson.description: Identify basic safety needs (clean water, safe food, clean environment).
Listen to short stories or talks about safety.
Complete sentences with words and expressions about hygiene and sanitation.

lessons.titreLesson: Writing and Talking About Environmental Safety

objectifsLesson.description: Write simple sentences about keeping the environment clean.
Use sequence markers/link words (first, then, next, finally).
Create a simple poster or slogan for a Health/Environment Club.

lessons.titreLesson: Types of Meals and Food Nutrients

objectifsLesson.description: Learn vocabulary: breakfast, lunch, dinner, snack, protein, carbohydrates, vitamins.
Name food groups (fruits, vegetables, grains, dairy, meat).
Read short simple texts or recipes with pictures about balanced diets.
Write or rearrange a simple recipe or daily menu.
Use sequence markers (first, then, after that, finally).
Listen to short speeches or talks on responsible feeding habits.
Explain why a meal is healthy or unhealthy.
Answer questions like Why is breakfast important?
Use interrogative words (why, what, how) to discuss food habits.
Write 4–5 sentences describing one day's balanced meals.
Use action verbs related to cooking and eating (eat, drink, cook, prepare).
Share and compare menus with classmates.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can identify rights and duties of a child, understand birth/nationality/marriage, describe national emblems, and talk about national holidays and customs.

objectifsLesson.description: Name basic rights of a child (right to education, health, protection, food, shelter).
Listen to short dialogues, speeches, or presentations about children's rights.
Read simple texts such as rules, regulations, or excerpts from the UN Charter.
Name basic duties (respect parents, help at home, attend school, obey rules).
Distinguish between a right and a duty.
Complete or rearrange short sentences about rights and duties.

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Giving Information About Rights and Duties

objectifsLesson.description: Ask and answer What are the rights of a child? / What must a child do?
Use present forms of regular verbs.
Write 3–4 sentences about one right and one duty of a child.

lessons.titreLesson: Vocabulary Related to Birth and Nationality

objectifsLesson.description: Learn words: birth, birth certificate, date of birth, place of birth, nationality, citizen.
Read and interpret simple charts, diagrams, tables, or forms.
Listen to announcements or news reports for specific information.
Learn words: marriage, marriage certificate, husband, wife, spouse, wedding.
Read simple birth and marriage certificates.
Fill out a diary, form, journal, or table about births, nationalities, or marriages.

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Answering About Personal Information

objectifsLesson.description: Ask and answer Where were you born? / What is your nationality? / Are you married?
Use the past forms of regular verbs (was born, lived, married).
Share personal thoughts and feelings about family and identity.
Name the national emblems: flag, anthem, motto, seal, coat of arms.
Recognize colors, symbols, and words associated with each emblem.
Listen to talks, interviews, news reports, or songs about emblems.
Describe the flag (colors, stripes, stars, or symbols).
Recite or sing parts of the national anthem.
Explain the meaning of the national motto in simple words.

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Giving Information About Emblems

objectifsLesson.description: Ask and answer What does the flag look like? / What is the motto?
Write simple statements, questions, and answers about emblems.
Read and interpret pictures, flyers, songs, or poems about emblems.
Name important national holidays (Independence Day, Youth Day, National Day).
Identify dates and meanings of each holiday.
Listen to announcements, radio or TV news reports, or interviews.
Describe common customs (traditional dress, greetings, ceremonies, food).
Read short stories, newspaper articles, sketches, calendars, or diaries.
Use the plural of regular nouns correctly (holidays, celebrations, traditions).

lessons.titreLesson: Expressing Likes, Dislikes, and Preferences About Holidays

objectifsLesson.description: Say I like / I don't like / I prefer about holidays and customs.
Present or exchange information about a favorite national holiday.
Write short postcard messages, greeting cards, or invitations related to holidays.
Write 4–5 sentences describing a national holiday (name, date, activities, food, clothes).
Use present and past forms of regular verbs (celebrate, dance, eat, wear).
Complete sentences with words and expressions about customs and cultural practices.

chapitres.competenceChapitre: The learner can understand news, entertainment media, make phone calls, send SMS/emails, and use a computer.

objectifsLesson.description: Identify different media sources: radio, television, newspapers, and online news.
Learn vocabulary: headline, article, news bar, caption, breaking news, current issues.
Read short newspaper articles, news bars, or captions.

lessons.titreLesson: Listening to and Reading Local News

objectifsLesson.description: Listen to local or community news from audio-visual media.
Identify key information (who, what, where, when).
Answer simple comprehension questions about a news item.

lessons.titreLesson: Asking and Giving Information About News

objectifsLesson.description: Ask and answer What happened? / Where did it happen?
Review past forms of regular verbs (happened, arrived, stopped).
Write or rearrange simple texts related to local or community news.
Name types of entertainment: music, films, videos, sketches, songs.
Learn vocabulary: lyrics, video clip, film, actor, singer, concert.
Listen to music, watch short videos, or listen to sketches.
Read short song lyrics, captions, advertisements, or brochures.
Identify the main topic or mood of a song or film.
Complete simple sentences with words from songs or dialogues.

lessons.titreLesson: Expressing Preferences, Likes, and Dislikes About Entertainment

objectifsLesson.description: Say I like / I love / I don't like / I prefer (pop music, action films).
Give simple reasons (because it is fun, interesting, boring, exciting).
Make short commentaries about a film or song.
Learn vocabulary: call, ring, answer, hang up, hello, goodbye, speak, listen.
Listen to short dialogues or advice on making and receiving calls.
Use polite expressions (May I speak to...? / Hold on, please. / Can I leave a message?).
Read and write short SMS messages.
Use abbreviations commonly used in SMS (e.g., thx, ok, cu later, msg).
Rearrange words or sentences to form a coherent SMS.
Identify parts of an email: To, From, Subject, Message.
Write a very short email (2–3 sentences).
Complete or rearrange dialogues related to making and receiving calls or emails.
Name basic parts: screen, keyboard, mouse, printer, CPU.
Learn vocabulary: turn on, turn off, click, type, save, print.
Read simple instructions, brochures, manuals, or articles about computers.

lessons.titreLesson: Following Instructions for Using a Computer

objectifsLesson.description: Listen to simple radio or television lessons or interviews about computers.
Follow simple instructions (Turn on the computer. Open a file. Type your name. Save).
Use the simple imperative (Click here. Press this button. Shut down properly).

lessons.titreLesson: Asking for and Giving Instructions About Computers

objectifsLesson.description: Ask How do I...? / What do I click? / Where do I save?
Give step-by-step instructions using sequence markers (first, then, next, finally).
Fill out simple tables, forms, or guidelines about using a computer.
